title: Short tree-like resolution from small proof space
formal: For \(\mu\) equal to resolution clause space CSpace or PCR monomial space \(MSpace_{K}\), does there exist a constant \(a\ge 1\) and \(C>0\) such that every unsatisfiable CNF F on \(n\ge 2\) variables satisfies \(\log _{2}(S_{T}(F)+1)\le C((\mu (F)+1)\log _{2}(n+1))^{a}\)? Determine the validity of this comparison in each of the two cases in the source’s Problem 5.1. For monomial space, K is an arbitrary fixed field and the constants may depend on K, but not on F or n. Here \(S_{T}\) is minimum tree-like resolution leaf count. The opposite comparison, bounding each space measure by logarithmic tree-like size up to these polynomial/logarithmic losses, is known.
context:
A configuration refutation can retain a clause, use it many times and discard it later. A tree-like refutation must duplicate reused derivations. The question asks how much tree size can grow when only a small working memory is needed.

The source proves equivalence when a proof’s space is multiplied by the logarithm of its length and then minimized over proofs. Removing that length penalty is precisely the missing step in this comparison; it is not the product of two separately minimized quantities.

The symbol ≈ does not mean equality or equality up to constants. A gap by a fixed polynomial, or by a polylogarithmic factor in n, is allowed. This convention is essential for understanding what would constitute a separation.

The source exhibits formulas with clause space four and quadratic tree-like size. Their logarithmic tree size is only \(O(\log  n)\), so that example does not violate the proposed comparison.
why: Would determine whether low working memory in propositional refutations fundamentally limits repeated work, clarifying strong size-space trade-offs and the cost of converting reusable proofs into trees.

sentences: The source compares working memory in refutations with the logarithm of minimum tree-like resolution size.
Its two memory measures are stored clauses in resolution and distinct monomials in polynomial calculus with resolution.
The comparison allows polynomial losses and powers of log n, so it is much coarser than a constant-factor identity.
A length-penalized version of space is already known to satisfy the comparison.
The unresolved issue is whether ordinary space can be substantially smaller on this scale.

definitions:
A literal is \(x_{i}\) or its negation \(
eg x_{i}\). A clause is a disjunction of literals and a CNF F is a finite conjunction of clauses over variables \(x_{1},\ldots ,x_{n}\); unsatisfiable means no Boolean assignment satisfies every clause. Resolution derives \(C\lor D\) from \(C\lor x_{i}\) and \(D\lor 
eg x_{i}\), and allows weakening from C to \(C\lor D\); input clauses can be used as axioms. A refutation derives the empty clause. A tree-like proof uses each derived occurrence as a premise at most once, duplicating occurrences when necessary; \(S_{T}(F)\) is the minimum number of leaves, rather than total literal count. A configuration proof starts with no stored clauses and at each step downloads an input clause, erases a stored clause, or adds a resolvent/weakening of clauses currently stored; it ends with the empty clause stored. \(CSpace(F)\) is the minimum, over such proofs with unrestricted length, of the maximum number of simultaneously stored clauses. For PCR fix K and use the polynomial ring \(K[x_{1},\ldots ,x_{n},y_{1},\ldots ,y_{n}]\), where \(y_{i}\) represents \(
eg x_{i}\). A line P means \(\mathrm{P}=0\). Logical axioms are \(z^{2}- z\) for each z among \(x_{i},y_{i}\) and \(x_{i}+y_{i}- 1\). The encoding of a clause is the product of its false-literal indicators: \(x_{i}\) contributes \(y_{i}\) and \(
eg x_{i}\) contributes \(x_{i}\). From P,Q derive \(\alpha \mathrm{P}+ eta Q\) for \(\alpha , eta \in K\); from P derive zP for any literal variable z. A PCR refutation derives 1. Its configurations may download axioms, erase lines or add an inference whose premises are stored. The monomial space of a configuration is the number of distinct formal monomials with nonzero coefficients occurring anywhere in its stored polynomials, counted once across all lines; coefficients and exponents are not separately charged. \(MSpace_{K}(F)\) is the minimum maximum monomial space over all PCR refutations. Every proof is finite and minima concern the specified syntactic systems. The source’s relation \(A\preceq B\) permits \(A(F)\le ((B(F))\log  n)^{O(1)}; \approx\) means both directions. The harmless +1 terms here cover one-leaf or other constant-size cases. No polynomial-length restriction is imposed on the space-minimizing proof.
answer_criterion: For each stated space measure, prove the universal polynomial/logarithmic simulation bound or refute it by showing that no constants C,a work for all unsatisfiable formulas (with K fixed in the PCR case). The two variants must be reported separately. A polynomial separation between raw measures does not refute a comparison that explicitly permits arbitrary polynomial and logarithmic factors.
